title: On-Demand Container Partitioning for Distributed ML
problem: Distributed ML training workloads have dynamic resource requirements that static container configurations cannot adapt to, leading to underutilization and prolonged training times.
motivation: Efficient resource utilization is critical for reducing training time and cost in large-scale distributed ML systems.
method: The system watches how much CPU, memory, and network bandwidth each container actually uses during training. When one container needs more resources while another has spare capacity, it automatically shifts resources between them without pausing the job. These adjustments happen continuously based on what the workload demands at each moment.
key_novelty: The system automatically shifts CPU, memory, and network resources between containers while training is running, adjusting in real-time to match what each container actually needs rather than using pre-set allocations.
contributions: On-demand container partitioning mechanism for distributed ML
Workload profiling and dynamic resource reallocation strategy
Empirical evaluation demonstrating training time improvements
System implementation supporting multi-node ML clusters
limitations: Not discussed in title; likely includes partitioning overhead and scalability constraints.
primary_theme: Dynamic container resource partitioning for ML
